retirements.title: The SQL verb as a predicate scanner
retirements.why: The retired form kept its own idea of which rows were in scope and could disagree with COUNT without saying so.
must_flag: | `SQL` | A **COUNT** command with `FOR <expr>` and optional `ALL` / `DELETED`. It does not execute SELECT statements; the name is historical. |
Use SQL COUNT FOR GPA >= 3.0 to count matching rows.
must_pass: | `SQL` | **A reserved name.** Retired as a scanner on 2026-09-04; it answers with direction to `COUNT` and `SQLSEL`. |

retirements.title: The SQLSEL legacy predicate-scan form
retirements.contract_status: supported (the STATEMENT surface ships; only the predicate form was withdrawn)
retirements.replaced_by: COUNT FOR <expr>, COUNT LIST, COUNT VERBOSE
retirements.why: Same defect as the SQL verb, one file over: a private deleted-row policy and a hand-rolled walk that consulted the shared selector zero times.
retirements.note: The published site says 2026-09-10 for this one. The source says 2026-09-09 twice, once in capitals. The source is the authority and the site should be corrected, not this file.
must_flag: The legacy predicate-scan form SQLSEL [COUNT] [FOR <expr>] is still accepted.
must_pass: SQLSEL COUNT FOR <expr> was retired on 2026-09-09; COUNT carries it now.

retirements.title: `SQL SELECT ...` as a way to run a SELECT statement
retirements.authority: src/cli/cmd_sql.cpp -- the SELECT redirect guard (header, line 16) is past tense; print_sql_reserved answers EVERY invocation
retirements.why: Retired with the scanner: the reserved verb gives one message for every invocation, so a page teaching `SQL SELECT` teaches a command that refuses.
must_flag: SQL SELECT custname, ordertotal FROM orders ORDER BY ordertotal LIMIT 20
must_pass: `SQLSEL` is the statement surface. The word `SQL` on its own is reserved and runs nothing.
SQLSEL SELECT SID,LNAME FROM SQLSTU ORDER BY LNAME DESC
